lines: It's very hot today, and sunny.
Tomorrow it will rain, and it'll be a bit cold.

adjective-predicate.title: Why "jīntiān hěn rè" and not "jīntiān shì rè"?
adjective-predicate.body: Adjectives in Chinese (rè, lěng, guì, piányi...) work as the verb of the sentence themselves — they don't need the verb shì (to be) in front. The hěn here hardly means "very" — it is just a linking word that is required before the adjective.

buta-not-very.title: 不太 (bú tài) — "not very"
buta-not-very.body: 不太 (bú tài) softens a negation, working like "not very" in English — instead of denying something completely, it says it isn't quite so, without being absolute.

hui-future-prediction.title: 会 (huì) — predicting the future
hui-future-prediction.body: Besides meaning "to know how to" (a learned skill, which you will see in Unit 15), 会 (huì) is also used to make predictions about what will happen — similar to "will" or "going to" in English.

trueFalse.claim: This sentence describes how a person is feeling.
trueFalse.whyNote: Wrong — 今天很热 describes the WEATHER (it is hot today), not how a person feels. "I'm hot" would be "我很热".
